title: "FTX Is Fine. Assets Are Fine." — What He Wrote the Day Before

lines.say: November seventh, two thousand twenty-two. Sam Bankman-Fried tweets to his customers.
lines.show: November 7, 2022. Sam Bankman-Fried tweets to his customers.

lines.say: FTX is fine. Assets are fine.

scene.q: FTX is fine. Assets are fine.
scene.cite: As quoted in the gov't sentencing memorandum

lines.say: FTX has enough to cover all client holdings.

scene.q: FTX has enough to cover all client holdings.
scene.cite: As quoted in the gov't sentencing memorandum

lines.say: But according to the trial evidence, the day before, he had written that FTX had enough to process about one third of remaining client assets.
Hours before the tweets, prosecutors said, he wrote in a group chat that FTX had three point nine billion of a twelve billion dollar total.
lines.show: Hours before the tweets, prosecutors said, he wrote in a group chat that FTX had $3.9 billion of a $12 billion total.

lines.say: Four days later, FTX filed for bankruptcy. A jury later convicted him on all seven counts.
lines.show: Four days later, FTX filed for bankruptcy. A jury later convicted him on all 7 counts.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
